config.gitWorkbench.git.path: Path to the Git executable. An empty value first inherits VS Code's `git.path`; otherwise the system Git in the current runtime environment is used. This value cannot be set by a workspace.
config.gitWorkbench.repositories.autoDet: Repository discovery scope: `openFolders` detects only opened folders; `subFolders` scans subdirectories; `off` uses manually added repositories only. The whole disk is never scanned.
config.gitWorkbench.repositories.scanDep: Maximum scan depth for `subFolders` mode, from 1 to 5. Higher values increase scan cost when opening large directories.
config.gitWorkbench.ui.followActiveRepos: In a multi-repository workspace, automatically follow the repository that owns the active editor file; when disabled, keep the user's selection.
config.gitWorkbench.ui.compactMode: `auto` adapts to available width; `compact` reduces row height and secondary information; `comfortable` keeps full information.
enum.gitWorkbench.ui.compactMode.compact: Reduce row height and secondary information.
config.gitWorkbench.graph.pageSize: Number of commits loaded at a time, from 50 to 1000. This does not limit total history.
config.gitWorkbench.graph.maxLanes: Maximum branch lanes drawn at once, from 8 to 200. More distant lanes are collapsed to limit layout cost.
config.gitWorkbench.graph.order: `topo` preserves topology; `date` orders by commit time; `authorDate` orders by author time.
config.gitWorkbench.graph.showWorkingTre: Show Working Tree, Index, and uncommitted-change nodes at the top of the graph.
config.gitWorkbench.graph.showRemoteBran: Show remote-tracking branches in the graph and reference list. Disabling this only hides them; it does not delete or modify refs.
config.gitWorkbench.graph.showTags: Show tags in the graph and reference list. Disabling this only hides them; it does not delete or modify tags.
config.gitWorkbench.graph.showStashes: Show stashes in the graph and reference list. Disabling this only hides them; it does not delete or pop stashes.
config.gitWorkbench.graph.showWorktrees: Show associated worktrees and whether they are dirty.
config.gitWorkbench.compare.defaultMode: `auto` uses merge-base only for branch-to-branch comparisons and Direct for other endpoint combinations; it can also be fixed to `direct` or `mergeBase`. The actual mode is always shown.
config.gitWorkbench.compare.ignoreWhites: `none` shows all whitespace; `eol` ignores line endings; `all` ignores all whitespace. This affects viewing only and does not change the actual patch. The workbench can override it with a session-level shortcut.
config.gitWorkbench.compare.renameDetect: `auto` detects within the performance budget; `on` always tries; `off` disables it. Degradation clearly shows additions and deletions.
config.gitWorkbench.compare.maxFileSizeM: Maximum single-file size for generating a full text diff, from 1 to 1024 MB. Larger files show metadata and statistics only.
config.gitWorkbench.compare.maxDiffLines: Maximum lines rendered initially for one diff, from 1000 to 200000. Larger diffs load in chunks and disable unnecessary decoration.
config.gitWorkbench.apply.defaultTarget: `prompt` asks every time; `worktree` writes the current workspace; `index` writes only the staging area; `newWorktree` applies in a new worktree.
config.gitWorkbench.commit.smartCommit: Whether to stage all tracked changes automatically when the index is empty. Disabled by default to prevent unreviewed content from entering a commit.
config.gitWorkbench.pull.strategy: `inherit` uses Git configuration and asks if it is unset; choose `prompt`, `ffOnly`, `merge`, or `rebase` to override it.
config.gitWorkbench.fetch.prune: `inherit` uses Git configuration; `on` prunes stale remote-tracking refs; `off` disables pruning. Local branches are never deleted.
config.gitWorkbench.remote.autoFetch: Whether to fetch in the background. It updates remote-tracking refs only; it does not automatically pull, merge, or modify the workspace.
config.gitWorkbench.remote.autoFetchInte: Automatic fetch interval, from 5 to 1440 minutes. It pauses while unfocused, sleeping, or performing write operations.
config.gitWorkbench.branch.dirtyWorktree: `prompt` asks; `keep` retains changes; `stash` creates a named stash; `newWorktree` creates a new worktree.
config.gitWorkbench.stash.includeUntrack: Whether new stashes include untracked files by default. The actual scope is still shown before execution.
config.gitWorkbench.conflict.autoOpen: `prompt` asks; `first` opens the first text conflict automatically; `never` shows only the banner and list.
enum.gitWorkbench.conflict.autoOpen.neve: Show the banner and list only.
config.gitWorkbench.safety.mode: `balanced` keeps normal operations short while previewing dangerous operations and creating checkpoints; `strict` adds confirmations and forbids rewriting published history. At runtime Global, Workspace, and Folder layers are read and the strictest value is used.
enum.gitWorkbench.safety.mode.balanced: Preview dangerous operations and create checkpoints.
enum.gitWorkbench.safety.mode.strict: Add confirmations and forbid rewriting published history.
config.gitWorkbench.safety.protectedBran: Protected branch globs. Normal commits and fast-forward pushes are allowed; deleting, resetting, rebasing, rewriting history, and force-pushing receive stronger checks. Rules are merged as a union across layers at runtime.
config.gitWorkbench.safety.publishedRewr: `deny` prohibits rewriting published history; `confirm` shows the impact, requires a second confirmation, and permits only an exact lease. At runtime all layers are read and the strictest value is used; there is no always-allow option.
enum.gitWorkbench.safety.publishedRewrit: Require impact preview, a second confirmation, and an exact lease.
config.gitWorkbench.safety.checkpointRet: Retention days for recovery checkpoints, from 1 to 365. Only internal recovery data in the current local or remote environment is cleaned.
config.gitWorkbench.safety.checkpointMax: Maximum recovery checkpoints per repository, from 5 to 500. Once exceeded, the oldest unpinned checkpoint is cleaned.

Total recovery-data limit for the current Extension Host, from 256 to 102400 MB. Pinned or active checkpoints are not automatically deleted; when space is insufficient, dangerous operations are blocked and the recovery center opens instead of creating an incomplete snapshot.
config.gitWorkbench.performance.profile: `auto` adjusts based on repository size and Git latency; `balanced` retains more information; `largeRepository` prioritizes performance.
enum.gitWorkbench.performance.profile.au: Adjust based on repository size and Git latency.
config.gitWorkbench.performance.maxCache: Global extension memory-cache limit, from 50 to 2048 MB. Once exceeded, LRU cleanup removes inactive repositories, old diffs, and graph pages.
config.gitWorkbench.performance.maxConcu: Global maximum read-only Git processes, from 1 to 8. Each repository has at most two read tasks, and writes are always serial.
config.gitWorkbench.logging.level: Local log level: `off/error/warn/info/debug/trace`. Trace must not record file contents, diffs, tokens, or credentials.
enum.gitWorkbench.logging.level.trace: Log trace messages without sensitive data.
config.gitWorkbench.diagnostics.redactPa: Hide usernames, absolute paths, repository names, and identifiable project information when exporting diagnostics. When disabled, path context needed for local export is retained; credentials, tokens, and URL passwords are always removed.
